outcome.summary: Confirmed bug in payment: Commit b7d87ca7 ("refactor: simplify card expiry comparison") in payment v1.4.0 changed the card-expiry check from strict '>' to '>=', causing cards expiring in the current month to be rejected during their entire expiration month — one month earlier than the documented rule ("a card stays valid through the last day of its expiration month").

results.title: Shoppers say their card is rejected as expired, but it's valid until the end of this month
results.text:
Since this morning several of our shoppers are told their card has expired at checkout, but their cards are valid until the end of this month. figma-shopper-03 and figma-shopper-11 both failed around 09:30. This is costing us orders.
A regression in payment v1.4.0 changed the card-expiry guard from strict '>' to '>=' in src/payment/charge.js. The guard now rejects a card when currentPeriod >= expiryPeriod, so a card expiring at the end of the current month is incorrectly flagged expired from the first day of that month. This contradicts the documented rule that a card stays valid through the last day of its expiration month.

data.reason: The symptoms differ in failure mode, scope, and affected shoppers. The open ticket is a specific, deterministic card-expiry validation bug: only shoppers whose card expires at the end of the current month are wrongly rejected, with an explicit "card expired" message, starting earlier in the morning (09:30). The new ticket is a broad, partial-failure outage: ~25% of all checkouts fail with a generic payment error starting at 11:05, affecting a share of all shoppers rather than a specific card-expiry subset, with no mention of an expiry message. A different error type and a different affected population indicate a different underlying problem, so linking them would be a wrong link.
data.new_problem: Since ~11:05, roughly 1 in 4 of all shoppers' checkouts fail with a generic "payment error"; the merchant reports no change on their side. It affects about a quarter of all checkouts across shoppers.
data.closest_problem: Since this morning, several shoppers are incorrectly told their card is expired at checkout even though it is valid until the end of the current month (e.g. figma-shopper-03, figma-shopper-11 around 09:30). Caused by a payment v1.4.0 regression in src/payment/charge.js where the expiry guard changed from '>' to '>=', rejecting cards whose expiry is the current month.

output.output:
# Payment Service

This service is responsible for processing and validating payments through the
application.

## Charge rules

`charge.js` rejects a charge when:

- the card number fails validation,
- the card is not VISA or MasterCard (other card types are not accepted),
- the card has expired: a card stays valid through the last day of its expiration month.

A declined charge is logged and returned to checkout as a gRPC error, with the reason in
the message.

## Local Build

Copy the `demo.proto` file to this directory and run `npm ci`

## Docker Build

From the root directory, run:

```sh
docker compose build payment
```

WHERE IT COMES FROM:
- src/payment/charge.js:86-90 (v1.4.0, /repo):
    const currentPeriod = currentYear * 12 + currentMonth;
    const expiryPeriod = year * 12 + month;
    if (currentPeriod >= expiryPeriod) { throw ... }
  The throw at charge.js:89 is the checkout-blocking error. It surfaces to the caller via the gRPC handler catch in src/payment/index.js:26-31 (logger.warn { err } 'Charge declined.', callback(err)) — index.js:26 is the only change on that line in this release (e0924cd0 changed the log call, not behaviour).

EXACT ERROR MESSAGE the code produces:
  'The credit card (ending \${lastFourDigits}) expired on \${month}/\${year}.'  (src/payment/charge.js:89)
  e.g. 'The credit card (ending 4242) expired on 9/2026.' for a card expiring in the current month.

WHAT CHANGED / WHICH COMMIT:
- Commit b7d87ca7 'refactor: simplify card expiry comparison' (Maya Patel, 2026-09-23), present between v1.3.0 and v1.4.0, changed the comparison operator from strict '>' to '>=':
    v1.3.0 (/prev src/payment/charge.js:86): if ((currentYear*12+currentMonth) > (year*12+month))
    v1.4.0 (/repo src/payment/charge.js:88): if (currentPeriod >= expiryPeriod)
  The other two commits in the release are non-behavioural: e0924cd0 adds a log message (src/payment/index.js:26) and 1ca185d8 adds docs (src/payment/README.md).

WHY IT IS A REGRESSION, NOT INTENDED BEHAVIOUR:
- It contradicts the documented rule added in this same release. README.md (v1.4.0, 'Charge rules') states: 'the card has expired: a card stays valid through the last day of its expiration month.' By that rule a card expiring in the current month must still be accepted; the '>=' test rejects it during its entire expiration month, one month too early.
- v1.3.0's strict '>' implemented that documented rule correctly (reject only when the current period is strictly after the expiry period). The commit is labelled a 'refactor' and was meant to be behaviour-preserving, but flipping '>' to '>=' is a semantic change.
- Effect matches the report: every shopper whose card expires in the current calendar month now fails checkout with the expiry error — a whole cohort of per-month-expiring cards, which plausibly accounts for the observed ~1-in-4 checkout failure rate. (The synthetic paymentFailure flag at charge.js:43-49 is unrelated: it is only active when the flag is > 0 and would affect all cards, not just expiring ones.)

FIX: change charge.js:88 back to a strict greater-than (currentPeriod > expiryPeriod) so cards remain valid through the last day of their expiration month, as the README requires."

evidence.observation: Commit b7d87ca7 'refactor: simplify card expiry comparison' (Maya Patel, 2026-09-23) changed the expiry test from `if ((currentYear * 12 + currentMonth) > (year * 12 + month))` to `const currentPeriod = ...; const expiryPeriod = ...; if (currentPeriod >= expiryPeriod)`.
git blame attributes lines 86-88 (currentPeriod/expiryPeriod declarations and the `>=` comparison) to commit b7d87ca7b by Maya Patel, 2026-09-23; line 89's throw predates it (75dc5aa9b, 2026-04-23).

v1.4.0 code: `const currentPeriod = currentYear * 12 + currentMonth; const expiryPeriod = year * 12 + month; if (currentPeriod >= expiryPeriod) { throw new Error(...expired...) }` — the throw at charge.js:89 is the checkout-blocking error.
Exact error message the code produces: 'The credit card (ending ${lastFourDigits}) expired on ${month}/${year}.'

README 'Charge rules' documents: 'the card has expired: a card stays valid through the last day of its expiration month.' A card expiring in the current month must therefore still be accepted, contradicting the '>=' test.
index.js:26 was changed by e0924cd0 to log a message (logger.warn 'Charge declined.', callback(err)) — a non-behavioural log change; the decline reason is propagated to checkout as a gRPC error.
The third commit in the release, 1ca185d8 'docs(payment): describe the charge rules', only adds docs to src/payment/README.md — non-behavioural.
The synthetic paymentFailure flag is unrelated: it is only active when the flag value is > 0 and would affect all cards, not specifically expiring ones.

data.hypothesis: Commit b7d87ca7 ("refactor: simplify card expiry comparison") regressed checkout by flipping the card-expiry comparison from strict '>' to '>=', so cards expiring in the current month are now rejected during their entire expiration month — one month earlier than the documented rule allows.

data.root_cause: Commit b7d87ca7 ("refactor: simplify card expiry comparison") in payment v1.4.0 changed the card-expiry check from strict '>' to '>=', causing cards expiring in the current month to be rejected during their entire expiration month — one month earlier than the documented rule ("a card stays valid through the last day of its expiration month").
data.customer_reply: We've identified the cause of the payment failures. A recent update to our payment service changed how card expiration dates are validated, causing cards whose expiry month is the current month to be incorrectly declined during the whole of that month. Our engineering team is working on a fix and will roll it back/out promptly. No action is needed on your side.
data.engineering_summary: Root cause: In payment v1.4.0, commit b7d87ca7 "refactor: simplify card expiry comparison" changed the expiry validation in src/payment/charge.js:86-89 from `(currentYear * 12 + currentMonth) > (year * 12 + month)` to `currentPeriod >= expiryPeriod`. This makes cards expiring in the current month be treated as expired for the entire month, contradicting the documented rule in README ("a card stays valid through the last day of its expiration month"). Code evidence (call c2) confirms the `>=` comparison throws at charge.js:89 with "The credit card (ending ...) expired on ..."; git blame (call c3) attributes lines 86-88 to b7d87ca7b. Production telemetry confirms the symptom: traces show payment v1.4.0 charge failures with "expired on 9/2026" (call h8/h9), 72 "Charge declined" warn logs on 09-27 (h31), and a spike in payment charge error spans after v1.4.0 (h25). No flag changes occurred (h3), ruling out a config incident. The other two commits in the release are non-behavioural (log message e0924cd0, docs 1ca185d8). Fix: revert the comparison to strict '>' (or compare only year/month such that the card is valid through the last day of its expiration month), then re-deploy.
